messages:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT alert - increased DNS resolution errors observed for hosted-api in eu-west-1. Error rate ~18% for last 5m, downstream 503s. Pager: P0. Runbook: geo-dns-failures. https://pd.company/INC12345

maya_ops: seeing it too — spike started ~10:04 UTC. Grafana: api-frontend 5xx up, healthcheck failures to eu-west origin. Quick dig from our probe: `;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 54123`

liam_network: Cloudflare resolver metrics show elevated SERVFAILs from our edge resolvers (eu). Route53 health checks also flapping for the eu-west origin. Could be upstream resolver churn + geoDNS policy picking bad region.

ollie_sre: Confirming Route53 geolocation routing is returning mixed answers. I ran `curl -v https://hosted-api.eu-west.example/status` from a few probes and saw connection reset/503 from origin fallback pool.

nora_eng: pasted dig +short @8.8.8.8 hosted-api.example.com A -> returns eu-central IP; @1.1.1.1 returns eu-west IP, but several resolvers returning SERVFAIL. Suspect resolver throttling or propagation lag combined with health check flaps.

sam_support: customer-facing: 12 tickets inbound so far, mostly EU customers seeing intermittent failures. CS triage asking for ETA; we should give initial impact statement.

ollie_sre: immediate mitigation plan (short):
- Route A: add explicit failover record to point traffic to eu-central LBs (bypass geolocation selection)
- Route B: lower TTL on the A record to 30s (note: TTL change will not help existing cached resolvers immediately)
- Route C: disable faulty Route53 health check triggers temporarily to stop oscillation
- Engage Cloudflare/Route53 support if resolver errors persist

maya_ops: I'm going to open the Route53 change as emergency change now. Applying a weighted record to force more traffic to eu-central. Command snippet:```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"hosted-api.example.com","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"force-eu-central","Weight":90,"TTL":30,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"35.196.11.22"}]}}]}'
```

liam_network: @maya_ops also ping Cloudflare support + Route53. I'll pull resolver logs and see if we have upstream error codes. Adding CF ticket now (case 789101).

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: emergency-route53-bypass (changeset id cs-2026-03-15-001). Will wait for approval from oncall.

ollie_sre: Approved. maya, go ahead. After change we should monitor:
- resolver error rate (5m window)
- 5xx rate on frontend
- Route53 health check state

nora_eng: attaching quick dig traces (from our edge probes):
```
;; QUERY: hosted-api.example.com IN A
;; AUTHORITY SECTION:
hosted-api.example.com. 60 IN SOA ns-1.example.net. admin.example.net. 2026031501 7200 900 1209600 60
;; Received 0 answers, status: SERVFAIL
```

maya_ops: change applied at 10:18 UTC. Weighting increased -> traffic to eu-central. Lowered TTL to 30. Disabling health-check auto-failover for eu-west to avoid flapping.

liam_network: Cloudflare acknowledged ticket, they see elevated upstream resolver timeouts from a subset of EDNS paths; they recommend traffic steering off the affected resolver sets. Working on a mitigation on their side.

sam_support: CS update ready to send: "We’re investigating intermittent DNS failures impacting EU customers. We’ve applied a mitigation to route traffic to healthy eu-central endpoints. Expect reduced errors within minutes. We’ll update here with ETA for full resolution." Want review?

ollie_sre: LGTM. Add note: start incident bridge for postmortem capture.

oncall_bot: Handoff reminder: current on-call (ollie_sre) handing to next shift (liam_network) at 10:35 UTC. Summary pinned: P0 DNS resolution spike for hosted-api in EU, mitigation applied (force route to eu-central), CF ticket opened.

liam_network: taking handoff. Next steps for me: watch resolver error rate for 30m, confirm CF mitigation, and if errors continue open escalation with Route53. Also coordinate with CS for status page message.

nora_eng: quick note: we may want to run a canary to ensure eu-central can handle extra capacity. I started a 1% traffic canary earlier — looks healthy but will increase to 10% after 5m if no errors.

maya_ops: canary increased to 10% at 10:24 UTC. No CPU/mem alarms. 5xx rate dropped to 2% in last 3m. Resolver errors trending down.

sam_support: posting status page update now: "Partial outage: DNS resolution issues causing intermittent 503s for EU customers. Mitigation applied to route traffic to healthy endpoints. Monitoring for recovery."

liam_network: Cloudflare follow-up: they’ve applied a temporary reroute around the affected resolvers. They recommend we keep Route53 bypass for 1–2 hours while they fully remediate.

ollie_sre: Agreed. We’ll keep bypass in place for 2 hours, then slowly revert once CF confirms stable. Assigning postmortem owner: nora_eng. PD incident remains open.

oncall_bot: Escalation log: paged ENG-SECURITY?false, Legal?false, Sales?true (CS asked). Tickets updated.

nora_eng: will own postmortem. I’ll gather timeline, dig traces, resolver metrics, and the Route53 change diff. Target to publish preliminary postmortem within 48h.

maya_ops: moving to monitoring mode. If anyone sees error rate >5% again, ping me and I’ll roll forward alternative routing (eu-west -> us-west).

sam_support: closing cluster of duplicate tickets with note about mitigation. Will reopen if customers continue to report.

liam_network: final note before I take over full watch: keep CF ticket (789101) active, ask for a postmortem / root cause from CF and Route53 if they confirm provider-side issue.

ollie_sre: thanks team. Marking this thread as the incident live coord. Handing off to @liam_network.

(reacts: :white_check_mark: by ollie_sre, :eyes: by liam_network)
